articles.title: This Was Ian Garry's One Shot #ufc
articles.description: Ian Garry may have just lost his only opportunity to fight Islam Makhachev for a UFC championship. Dana White has suggested that Garry may never fight for a UFC title again — and that another championship matchup with Islam could be even less likely. Chael Sonnen believes Garry's performance inside the Octagon deserves credit. But there's one thing he can't stop thinking about: why was Ian so concerned with earning Islam's respect? Garry spent valuable moments during and after the fight praising Islam, embracing him, and treating him like a friend rather than the man standing between him and the championship. Chael doesn't have a problem with psychological warfare. In fact, he believes trying to convince an opponent that you're his friend before ultimately attacking is completely fair game. But that's not what Chael believes happened here. The final embrace came after the final bell — and Chael points out that those seconds matter in a championship fight. If Islam remains champion, Garry may have to wait a very long time for another opportunity. And that's why Chael believes this could become the kind of mistake that keeps a fighter awake at night. Garry fought well. But did he waste the most important moments of his career? #IanGarry #IslamMakhachev #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #DanaWhite #UFCNews #MMAAnalysis #UFCChampionship #CombatSports

articles.title: Gable Steveson Is Built for Combat #ufc
articles.description: Gable Steveson is back — and Chael Sonnen believes we're watching an athlete unlike almost anyone he's ever seen. Steveson's weight is reportedly down to 242 pounds, a significant change for someone who was a massive athlete throughout his youth and college wrestling career. Chael compares Gable's physical gifts to elite combat athletes like Jon Jones and Jordan Burroughs, pointing out just how unusual Steveson's combination of athleticism, size, and explosiveness really is. But that's only part of the conversation. Chael also breaks down an incredible moment between Henry Cejudo and Merab Dvalishvili, where Cejudo defended against Merab's attacks before finding the opening that ended the match. It raises a bigger question: Do we need Henry Cejudo vs. Merab 3? Or should these two settle their rivalry in wrestling? Chael explains why he was impressed by Merab for putting himself in that situation — and why the possibility of another Cejudo-Merab matchup is so compelling. From Gable Steveson's return to one of MMA's most fascinating wrestling rivalries, this clip is all about elite athletes, combat sports, and what happens when world-class wrestlers collide. #GableSteveson #HenryCejudo #MerabDvalishvili #UFC #MMA #Wrestling #ChaelSonnen #JordanBurroughs #CombatSports #WrestlingNews

articles.title: Paddy Pimblett Gained 34 Pounds. So What?
articles.description: For a limited time, our listeners get 50% off FOR LIFE, Free Shipping, AND 3 Free Gifts at Mars Men at https://www.mengotomars.com Paddy Pimblett made the lightweight limit. Then he stepped into the Octagon significantly heavier. Does that make him a “weight bully,” or does it mean he simply played by the rules? Pimblett revealed that he weighed 190 pounds in the cage against Benoît Saint Denis after officially weighing 156 pounds, a 34-pound increase between the weigh-in and fight night. Chael challenges the assumption that gaining that much weight automatically creates an advantage. Carrying additional weight comes with consequences, and making 155 pounds requires enormous discipline, sacrifice and preparation in the first place. The larger question is whether MMA's weigh-in system makes sense at all. If regulators truly want to discourage extreme weight cutting, there are already examples of how to do it. But as long as the rules allow fighters time to rehydrate, athletes are going to search for every competitive advantage available. Paddy followed the rules and made the contracted weight. Chael explains why calling him a bully for doing it misses the point entirely. articles.title: I Disagree with Daniel Cormier
articles.description: Should a fighter really be punished for jumping on the cage after a victory? Daniel Cormier says let them celebrate. Chael sees it differently. According to the account Chael discusses, multiple fighters had pay withheld after cage celebrations triggered action from the Nevada State Athletic Commission. Chael's point isn't that fighters shouldn't enjoy their moment. It's that if a commission has a rule, it can't simply decide when that rule matters and when it doesn't. And there are real reasons to take the danger seriously. Chael recalls seeing a fighter attempt a celebratory backflip and land on a cameraman, breaking his leg. He also tells the story of Dan Henderson being encouraged to show more emotion after winning in PRIDE, only to injure his ACL during the celebration. This isn't about taking away a fighter's moment. It's about safety, liability and consistently enforcing the rules already on the books. If the rule is bad, change it. But until then, Chael argues you can't simply pretend it doesn't exist. articles.title: Fluffy Hernandez Lost… And I’m MORE Impressed
articles.description: Losing is never the goal. But if you're going to lose a fight, Anthony “Fluffy” Hernandez just showed you how to do it. Gregory “Robocop” Rodrigues defeated Hernandez by unanimous decision in the UFC Sacramento main event, handing Fluffy his second consecutive loss. But Chael believes the result doesn't tell the full story of what Hernandez showed inside the Octagon. Hernandez stayed composed, fought every round and continued competing instead of allowing earlier setbacks to dictate the rest of his performance. After putting together one of the most impressive runs in the middleweight division, Chael doesn't believe one more loss suddenly means Fluffy should be pushed down the card. It also raises a larger question about MMA: Do we actually know who the best fighter is? Unlike traditional sports, there isn't a tournament bracket that guarantees every top competitor eventually has to go through every other contender. Sometimes opportunity, timing and matchmaking shape history just as much as talent. Chael explains why Hernandez remains a compelling middleweight and why Rodrigues' victory deserves just as much respect. #ChaelSonnen #AnthonyHernandez #GregoryRodrigues #UFC #MMA Bad Guy Inc merch now available at https://BadGuyInc.com Click here to subscribe: https://bit.ly/3FrHIPK Follow me on IG: https://bit.ly/3HY7BIE Follow me on Twitter: https://bit.ly/3tvY5J7 Follow me on Threads https://www.threads.com/@sonnench

articles.title: Islam Is NOT Too Small for 170 #ufc
articles.description: Chael Sonnen has heard enough about Islam Makhachev supposedly being too small for 170 pounds. His response is simple: Islam and Ian Garry weighed exactly 170 pounds the day before their fight. So where is the size disadvantage? Chael argues that fans continue to treat Islam's move from lightweight to welterweight as though he's somehow competing against significantly larger men. But once both fighters step on the scale and weigh the same, the argument becomes much harder to defend. Chael also points out the inconsistency in MMA's size discussions. Fighters routinely compete against opponents who are significantly heavier or lighter in other circumstances, yet Islam's move from 155 to 170 continues to receive disproportionate attention. And there's another important detail: Islam has already proven he can compete at 170. He's not entering the division for the first time. He's already won a UFC championship at welterweight. So why are we still using size as an excuse? Chael believes the bigger issue is that people are trying to explain away why Islam doesn't finish every opponent, as though fighting under a time limit somehow counts against him. But if Islam is the champion, that's exactly what the belt represents. He has to win under the rules. And if he's being called the greatest fighter on the planet, the size argument shouldn't be necessary. #IslamMakhachev #IanGarry #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #UFCNews #MMAAnalysis #Welterweight #UFC170 #CombatSports

articles.title: What Happens If Tom Aspinall Can’t Fight? #ufc
articles.description: What happens if Tom Aspinall can't make the fight with Alex Pereira? Chael Sonnen explains the complicated situation developing at heavyweight — and why the UFC itself may be divided over what to do with Tom's championship. If Tom and Pereira can't get the fight done, the expectation is that Curtis Blaydes could step in against Pereira. But that creates an immediate question: What belt are they fighting for? Would it be for the undisputed heavyweight championship, or would Pereira be defending an interim title? According to Chael, there are reportedly people within the UFC who are split on whether Tom should even be stripped of the championship. The circumstances matter because Tom was injured during an actual UFC fight, in front of the world, rather than suffering an injury in training. That has created more willingness to give him some grace. But regardless of what happens, there are now multiple potential paths forward. If Tom and Pereira are medically cleared and the commissions approve the matchup, that's the fight everyone wants. And if the UFC needs a backup plan, Chael believes Curtis Blaydes vs. Alex Pereira could make sense as a No. 1 contender fight on the same card. The heavyweight title picture is getting complicated. #TomAspinall #AlexPereira #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #UFCHeavyweight #UFCNews #MMAAnalysis #HeavyweightMMA #CombatSports

articles.title: It’s time to accept Din Thomas’s apology #ufc
articles.description: Chael Sonnen believes Dean Thomas delivered the perfect apology. There's a major difference between simply saying "I'm sorry" and actually taking responsibility for what happened. According to Chael, Dean didn't just apologize — he explained what he did wrong, acknowledged that he took away from Jillian's moment, and identified what he was going to do differently moving forward. Most importantly, Dean was willing to take real action. He even described himself as the weakness in the camp and announced a major decision that demonstrated just how seriously he was taking responsibility. Chael believes that level of accountability makes the sincerity impossible to ignore. And now Chael is responding publicly. After going back and watching the fight, Chael says he came away extremely proud of Jillian. He didn't believe she ever backed down, and he felt she performed very well despite everything surrounding the situation. So Chael accepts Dean Thomas' apology — in full. At the same time, Chael admits Dean may be being too hard on himself. This is a fascinating look at what a genuine apology actually looks like when someone is willing to accept responsibility, acknowledge the impact of their actions, and make a meaningful change. #ChaelSonnen #DeanThomas #MMA #UFC #MMAAnalysis #UFCNews #CombatSports #MMACommunity #FightGame

articles.title: Who Can Take Justin Gaethje’s Belt? #ufc
articles.description: If Justin Gaethje's next fight really is his last, the UFC has a problem. Chael Sonnen believes that if Gaethje is considering retirement, there's a very real possibility that his next fight could be his final appearance in the Octagon. And if that's the case, the stakes become even higher. The UFC doesn't want its champion walking away with the belt. That's where the potential matchups with Paddy Pimblett and Ilia Topuria come into play. If Chael had to choose between the two as Gaethje's next opponent, he'd lean toward Paddy — largely because of the damage and recovery involved. But the bigger question is which fighter is actually equipped to take the belt away from Gaethje. Gaethje is one of the most dangerous punchers in the sport. His pressure, durability, and power make every matchup a problem, especially when there's a championship on the line. And if the UFC knows this could be his last fight, Chael believes the people making the matchup have one job: Get the belt back. They can't publicly say that's the objective, but that's exactly what the situation demands. So between Paddy Pimblett and Ilia Topuria, who is best equipped to beat Justin Gaethje and prevent him from walking away as champion? #JustinGaethje #PaddyPimblett #IliaTopuria #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #UFCNews #MMAAnalysis #BMF #CombatSports

articles.title: Conor McGregor’s Infamous Grand Arrival Confrontation | This Day in MMA: Aug. 22
articles.description: This Day in MMA: Conor McGregor’s Infamous Grand Arrival Confrontation | Aug. 22 August 22, 2017. Four days before Floyd Mayweather and Conor McGregor, the Grand Arrival at T-Mobile Arena fell apart on the red carpet. McGregor had already promised a short night — he was struggling to give Mayweather two rounds. Then he and Floyd had to be pulled apart by their own security. And then Paulie Malignaggi walked up on him. Malignaggi had sparred McGregor in that camp and walked out of it, and the photos went out anyway. He wanted an answer: "Did you bring your balls, Conor?" He had a prediction, too — McGregor was going to fold again on Saturday. Across the same carpet, Floyd Mayweather was calmer, and more specific: this fight wouldn't go the distance. If you're gonna bet, bet it won't go. Four days later he stopped him in the tenth. articles.description: Daniel Cormier IS BACK after UFC 329 made headlines with Paddy Pimblett, Max Holloway, and Gable Stevenson all facing potential money being withheld because of jumping on the cage after their victories. Technically speaking, rules do not allow fighters to exit the cage after a victory, but DC argues that the emotion of a massive victory and given the stakes of all three of their fights, the rule NEEDS TO CHANGE. Paddy Pimblett had a nasty first-round submission of Benoit Saint-Denis, Max avenged a loss vs. Conor McGregor, and Gable made his UFC debut with an incredible knockout victory. articles.title: 22 Years Ago Today: Randy Couture Took the Title Back at 41 🏆
articles.description: 22 Years Ago Today: Randy Couture Took the Title Back at 41 August 21, 2004. MGM Grand. Randy Couture and Vitor Belfort had already fought twice, and neither fight had settled anything. The first time, back at UFC 15 in 1997, Couture stopped him with punches in round one. The second, in January 2004, Belfort's glove caught Couture's eyelid forty-nine seconds in — the doctor waved it off and Belfort walked out with the light heavyweight title. They called the rubber match Unfinished Business. This time there was no accident. Couture controlled all three rounds, and at the end of the third the doctor looked at Belfort's eye and ended it. Forty-one years old, and Randy Couture was champion again. Two wins to one. Three fights, three finishes. Nobody ever needed a fourth. Twenty-two years ago today. articles.title: Who Is Really Next for Islam Makhachev? #ufc
articles.description: Carlos Prates says he's next for Islam Makhachev. But Chael Sonnen isn't convinced that's how this should play out. There's now a potential problem at the top of the division: Carlos Prates and Michael Morales both have legitimate arguments to be next in line. One suggestion has been to simply put them against each other and let the winner become the undisputed No. 1 contender. Sounds logical. But Chael sees a major downside. If two legitimate contenders fight each other, you eliminate one potential title fight. And if the UFC doesn't need them to fight each other to determine who's next, why remove one of those options? There's also the question of what happens to Islam while that fight takes place. If Morales and Prates have to fight first, Islam could potentially be sitting on the shelf while the UFC determines his next challenger. Chael's preference is clear: he doesn't want to eliminate either contender. Morales has an especially strong case. Chael points out that it was reportedly Dana White who told Morales he was next following his huge victory at Madison Square Garden. Prates is certainly dangerous and has plenty of support inside the UFC. But Chael believes Morales is the guy who should be fighting Islam. So who actually gets the next title shot? And should Morales and Prates really be forced to eliminate each other first? #IslamMakhachev #MichaelMorales #CarlosPrates #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #UFCNews #MMAAnalysis #UFCTitle #CombatSports
